candidate_method.aggregate: minimum anchor score over all target anchors and physical channels
candidate_method.anchor_score: minimum of amplitude_component and spectral_component, each lower-bounded at zero; values above one are retained as diagnostics
candidate_method.rationale: Both components compare attack to that signal's own local post-attack tail. This suppresses global gain/root/timbre dependence while retaining sensitivity to envelope rounding/attenuation and onset-only low-pass damage.
candidate_method.spectral_component: ((candidate early derivative_rms/early_rms)/(candidate late derivative_rms/late_rms))/((target early derivative_rms/early_rms)/(target late derivative_rms/late_rms))

cases.description: two-onset target; strongest onset survives while second target onset is removed
two-channel target; one physical channel preserves attack and the other loses it

decision_rule.cross_platform: portable raw ratios absolute 1e-7 / relative 1e-5; classification exact
decision_rule.damaged: all damage/adversarial controls must have transient score < 0.4 or be rejected by an unchanged independent hard gate whose measurement directly demonstrates the declared damage
decision_rule.edge: finite deterministic output; inactive target may report neutral ratio 1.0 and rely on existing activity gates
decision_rule.preserved: all five preserved controls must have transient score >= 0.4 and no new hard-gate rejection caused by transient method
decision_rule.raw_evidence: retain anchors, per-anchor amplitude/spectral components, aggregate ratio, and baseline v1 ratio
decision_rule.threshold: 0.4 is frozen from ValidationPolicy; do not tune after outcomes

reason_for_revision: The frozen envelope-rise candidate is rejected before production because gain-normalized smoothing/attenuation can preserve local normalized rise. This revision adds within-signal onset-versus-tail normalization and attack-specific spectral contrast without changing the 0.4 eligibility threshold or fixture labels.
